rationales.quote: And where are you in ARR now? Sorry.
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks for current ARR to assess the company's trajectory against its stated revenue targets.

rationales.quote: a very, very active engaged entry point
rationales.explanation: She views the passionate equestrian market as a strong initial wedge from which the company can learn and expand.

rationales.quote: You know this market cold
rationales.explanation: She credits the founders' deep knowledge of the equestrian market as an investment strength.

rationales.quote: I'm a little uncomfortable with 10 post.
rationales.explanation: Jillian considers the proposed $10 million post-money valuation uncomfortable for the company's current stage.

rationales.quote: That's not palatable to me.
rationales.explanation: She reiterates that the proposed valuation is unacceptable at this stage.

rationales.quote: they showed me the numbers on dog owners, and they showed me the numbers on knitters
rationales.explanation: A prior pitch involving a passionate niche market shaped her view that seemingly narrow audiences can support compelling businesses.

rationales.quote: if you have a fanatical market, you can sell them anything
rationales.explanation: Her prior experience with a fanatical niche that succeeded reinforces her positive view of RideIQ's passionate customer base.

rationales.quote: I'm not gonna do it if it's not six.
rationales.explanation: She makes six million the maximum valuation at which she will invest.

rationales.quote: First of all, you have a lot of competition.
rationales.explanation: During diligence, Jillian flags the crowded competitive environment and asks why RideIQ will win.

rationales.quote: I don't think anyone at this point in time would come in with anything higher than six.
rationales.explanation: She believes the company's current stage does not support a valuation above six million.

rationales.quote: I feel there's a lack of defensibility here
rationales.explanation: Jillian declines to invest because she does not see a sufficiently defensible product or competitive position.

rationales.quote: I'm a little uncomfortable with 10 post.

rationales.quote: I love a good fanatical market.

rationales.quote: they showed me the numbers on dog owners, and they showed me the numbers on knitters
rationales.explanation: She recounts a prior niche-market pitch that informs her current view of passionate customer segments.

rationales.quote: if you have a fanatical market, you can sell them anything
rationales.explanation: Her experience of passing on a successful niche business taught her to value fanatical markets, supporting her RideIQ investment.

rationales.quote: I'm not gonna do it if it's not six.
rationales.explanation: She makes a $6 million valuation a condition of investing.

rationales.quote: First of all, you have a lot of competition.
rationales.explanation: During diligence, she flags the number of competing equestrian coaching apps as a material concern.

rationales.quote: and what is the valuation?

rationales.quote: I don't think anyone at this point in time would come in with anything higher than six.
rationales.explanation: She believes the company cannot presently support an investment valuation above $6 million.

rationales.quote: And where are you in ARR now? Sorry.
rationales.explanation: She asks for current ARR after hearing the founders' future revenue targets.

rationales.quote: The point is a very, very active engaged entry point.
rationales.explanation: She sees the engaged equestrian market as a strong initial wedge before expansion into other fanatical markets.

rationales.quote: You know this market cold.
rationales.explanation: She considers the founders' deep knowledge of the equestrian market a major investment strength.

rationales.quote: I'm a little uncomfortable with 10 post.
rationales.explanation: She objects to the proposed $10 million post-money valuation.

rationales.quote: That's not palatable to me.
rationales.explanation: She reiterates that the proposed valuation is unacceptable to her.

rationales.quote: I love a good fanatical market.
rationales.explanation: She identifies an intensely committed niche audience as a favorable market-entry characteristic.

rationales.quote: they showed me the numbers on dog owners, and they showed me the numbers on knitters
rationales.explanation: She recounts a prior niche-market pitch that informs her current view of passionate customer segments.

rationales.quote: if you have a fanatical market, you can sell them anything
rationales.explanation: Her experience of passing on a successful niche business taught her to value fanatical markets, supporting her RideIQ investment.

rationales.quote: I'm not gonna do it if it's not six.
rationales.explanation: She makes a $6 million valuation a condition of investing.

rationales.quote: First of all, you have a lot of competition.
rationales.explanation: During diligence, she flags the number of competing equestrian coaching apps as a material concern.

rationales.quote: and what is the valuation?
rationales.explanation: She reconfirms the proposed valuation during diligence before assessing whether it is supportable.

rationales.quote: I don't think anyone at this point in time would come in with anything higher than six.
rationales.explanation: She believes the company cannot presently support an investment valuation above $6 million.

rationales.quote: I need to understand. A little bit more about the competitive landscape.
rationales.explanation: She declines to invest immediately because she needs further diligence to assess the competitive landscape.

rationales.quote: I feel there's a lack of defensibility here, and I'm not quite sure how you're going to win.
rationales.explanation: She explicitly links her refusal to uncertainty about RideIQ's defensibility and ability to beat competitors.

validated_extraction.notes: All supplied target turns were reviewed exactly once; non-rationale greetings, fragments, jokes, confirmations, and bare commitments were excluded.
